stem:
The diagram shows trapezium $PQRS$ with $PQ\parallel SR$. Angle $QPS=65^{\circ}$. Farhan wants angle $PSR$ on the same non-parallel side as angle $QPS$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Angle $PSR=65^{\circ}$ because angle $PSR$ must equal angle $QPS$ in a trapezium.
Angle $PSR$ cannot be found from the parallel sides alone.
Angle $PSR=115^{\circ}$ because the angles on the same non-parallel side between the parallel sides add to $180^{\circ}$.
Angle $PSR=65^{\circ}$ because $PQ$ equals $SR$ on the diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: With PQ∥SR, co-interior angles on the same non-parallel side PS add to 180°, so angle PSR=180−65=115°. Equal corresponding angles confuse the parallel-side property. Saying the angle cannot be found omits the co-interior sum. Equality of PQ and SR is not given and is not the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle into labelled trapezium PQRS with PQ∥SR and marked 65°.
